title: Follow-up is a journey, not a chase
learningGoal: Know what needs to happen between an enquiry and a booking.

sections.title: What a Lead Wants to Know

items.title: Did you receive my message?
items.description: A lead wants confirmation that their enquiry was received and is being handled.

items.title: Can you help me?
items.description: They need to know if your service or product fits their specific situation.

items.title: What should I do next?
items.description: A clear next step removes confusion and moves the conversation forward.

items.title: 1. Capture
items.description: A contact submits a form or makes an enquiry.

items.title: 2. Respond
items.description: Send a friendly acknowledgement promptly.

items.title: 3. Invite
items.description: Offer one clear way to book a call or take the next step.

items.title: 4. Check
items.description: Allow time and check for a reply or booking.

items.title: 5. Follow up
items.description: Send a single relevant reminder if there has been no response or booking.

items.title: Write the exact question
items.description: What is your ideal lead asking when they fill out your form?

items.title: Write one helpful sentence
items.description: Answer that question in a single sentence that reassures and guides them.

keyPoint: A lead wants to know three things: Did you receive my message? Can you help me? What should I do next? The five-step formula is Capture, Respond, Invite, Check, Follow up.

actionSteps.title: Identify your lead's primary question
actionSteps.description: Write the exact question your ideal lead is asking when they fill out your form.

actionSteps.title: Write a one-sentence answer
actionSteps.description: Create one helpful sentence that answers their question and moves them forward.

actionSteps.title: Review the five-step formula
actionSteps.description: Check your current follow-up process against Capture, Respond, Invite, Check, Follow up.

quizzes.question: What are the three things a lead wants to know after submitting an enquiry?

options.option_text: Price, features, and competitors
Did you receive my message? Can you help me? What should I do next?
How fast, how cheap, how good
Who are you, what do you do, why should I care

quizzes.explanation: A lead wants to know: Did you receive my message? Can you help me? What should I do next? A useful response answers these three questions without overwhelming them.

quizzes.question: What is the correct order of the five-step follow-up formula?

options.option_text: Invite, Capture, Respond, Check, Follow up
Capture, Respond, Invite, Check, Follow up
Capture, Check, Respond, Invite, Follow up
Respond, Capture, Invite, Follow up, Check

quizzes.explanation: The five-step formula is: 1. Capture (form submission), 2. Respond (acknowledgement), 3. Invite (clear next step), 4. Check (allow time), 5. Follow up (single reminder if needed).

quizzes.question: How many follow-up reminders should you send if there is no response?

options.option_text: As many as it takes until they reply
Three reminders over two weeks
A single relevant reminder
None — never follow up

quizzes.explanation: The formula recommends sending a single relevant reminder if there has been no response or booking. Multiple unsolicited follow-ups can feel like chasing and damage trust.

title: Connect the starting point
learningGoal: Start a workflow when the correct form is submitted.

items.title: Open Sites → Forms
items.description: Review your enquiry form and confirm name and email fields are present.

items.title: Confirm Required Fields
items.description: Ensure the form captures the minimum information needed for follow-up.

items.title: Open Automation → Workflows
items.description: Create a workflow from scratch.

items.title: Name It Clearly
items.description: Use a descriptive name like M17 | Consultation enquiry | Follow-up.

items.title: Add Form Submitted Trigger
items.description: Select the trigger Form Submitted, filter Form is, and choose only the intended enquiry form.

items.title: Save Unpublished
items.description: Keep the workflow unpublished until you have tested it thoroughly.

items.title: Prevent Wrong Triggers
items.description: Without the filter, the wrong form could start a sales follow-up, such as a customer service form or feedback survey.

items.title: Exercise for Consultants
items.description: Choose the form used for strategy enquiries and note its exact name.

keyPoint: Create a workflow with the Form Submitted trigger, filter by the exact enquiry form, and keep it unpublished until tested. The filter prevents unrelated forms from triggering your sales sequence.

actionSteps.title: Review your enquiry form
actionSteps.description: Open Sites → Forms and confirm your enquiry form has name and email fields.

actionSteps.title: Create a new workflow
actionSteps.description: Open Automation → Workflows and create a workflow named M17 | Consultation enquiry | Follow-up.

actionSteps.title: Add and filter the trigger
actionSteps.description: Add Form Submitted trigger, filter Form is, and select only your intended enquiry form.

quizzes.question: What trigger starts the follow-up workflow?

options.option_text: Contact Created
Form Submitted
Email Opened
Appointment Booked

quizzes.explanation: The workflow starts with the Form Submitted trigger, filtered to only the intended enquiry form. This ensures the right form submissions begin the follow-up sequence.

quizzes.question: Why should you filter the Form Submitted trigger by a specific form?

options.option_text: To make the workflow run faster
So unrelated forms do not trigger the sales sequence
To reduce the number of workflow executions
Because HighLevel requires it

quizzes.explanation: Without filtering by form, any form submission — including customer service forms or feedback surveys — could trigger your sales follow-up sequence. The filter ensures only the intended enquiry form starts the workflow.

quizzes.question: When should you publish the workflow?

options.option_text: Immediately after creating it
Only after successful end-to-end testing
After adding the first email action
When the client asks for it

quizzes.explanation: Keep the workflow unpublished until you have tested it thoroughly. Publishing before testing risks sending incorrect or incomplete follow-ups to real prospects.

title: Write the first useful email
learningGoal: Make the first reply helpful and human.

items.title: Acknowledge the Enquiry
items.description: Confirm you received their details and express interest in learning more.

items.title: Offer a Clear Next Step
items.description: Provide one way to book a call — a tested calendar booking link.

items.title: Invite Replies
items.description: Let them know they can reply with a question if they are not ready to book.

items.title: Subject: Thanks for getting in touch
items.description: Hi {{contact.first_name}}, Thanks for your enquiry. I have received your details and would be pleased to learn more about what you are working on. If you would like to talk through your goals, you can choose a convenient time here: [Insert your tested calendar booking link]. If you have a question first, simply reply to this email. Best, [Your name]

items.title: Verify Sender Details
items.description: Check sender name, sender address, and merge field preview.

items.title: Test the Booking URL
items.description: Confirm the link opens the intended calendar before using it in a live email.

items.title: Avoid False Claims
items.description: Do not claim you personally reviewed an enquiry if that has not happened.

keyPoint: The first email should acknowledge the enquiry, offer one clear way to book, and invite questions. Always test your booking link and verify sender details before sending.

actionSteps.title: Draft your first email
actionSteps.description: Write a short, helpful email that acknowledges the enquiry and offers a booking link.

actionSteps.title: Test your booking link
actionSteps.description: Click the calendar link to confirm it opens the correct booking page.

actionSteps.title: Preview merge fields
actionSteps.description: Check that {{contact.first_name}} and other merge fields display correctly.

quizzes.question: What is the single action you want the prospect to take after reading the first email?

options.option_text: Visit your website homepage
Book a call or reply with a question
Follow you on social media
Download a free guide

quizzes.explanation: The first email should have one clear call to action: book a call using the calendar link, or reply with a question if they need more information first.

quizzes.question: Why should you test the booking URL before including it in the email?

options.option_text: To make the email look more professional
To confirm it opens the intended calendar and works correctly
Because HighLevel requires URL verification
To track click-through rates

quizzes.explanation: Testing the booking URL ensures it opens the correct calendar, the times display properly, and the prospect can actually complete a booking. A broken link defeats the purpose of the follow-up.

quizzes.question: What should you avoid claiming in the first email?

options.option_text: That you received their enquiry
That you personally reviewed their enquiry if you have not
That you would be pleased to learn more
That they can reply with a question

quizzes.explanation: Do not claim you personally reviewed an enquiry if that has not happened. Automated emails should be honest about their nature to maintain trust with the prospect.

title: Add timing and response checks
learningGoal: Avoid sending reminders to people who have already engaged.

items.title: Insert a Wait Action
items.description: Add Wait after the first email. Start with 1 day as a training example, not a universal best timing rule.

items.title: Timing Is Context-Dependent
items.description: The right wait time depends on your audience, offer, and industry. Test and adjust.

items.title: Add Response Checks
items.description: Before any reminder, add a decision or exit mechanism that checks whether the contact has replied or booked.

items.title: Review Available Conditions
items.description: Check your account's available workflow conditions and appointment settings.

items.title: End the Path if Engaged
items.description: If the contact replied or booked, end the sales reminder path or remove them from the follow-up workflow.

items.title: Subject: Would a short call be useful?
items.description: Hi {{contact.first_name}}, Just following up on your enquiry. If a short conversation would help you decide on the next step, here is my calendar: [Insert booking link]. No pressure if the timing is not right. You can also reply with a question. Best, [Your name]

items.title: Send Only One Reminder
items.description: Send one helpful reminder, then end the workflow. A separate Customer Booked Appointment workflow can handle confirmations.

items.title: Wait Does Not Auto-Stop
items.description: A simple 1-day Wait does not automatically stop messages when someone books. Configure this logic explicitly.

items.title: SMS Requires Consent
items.description: Do not use SMS without suitable consent, registration, and compliance checks.

items.title: Exercise for Trainers
items.description: Describe two cases when a person should NOT receive the reminder.

keyPoint: A Wait action does not automatically know when someone has booked. You must explicitly configure reply checks, booking checks, or removal logic before sending any reminder.

actionSteps.title: Add a Wait action
actionSteps.description: Insert a 1-day Wait after the first email in your workflow.

actionSteps.title: Add response or booking checks
actionSteps.description: Configure conditions to check if the contact has replied or booked before sending a reminder.

actionSteps.title: Draft one reminder email
actionSteps.description: Write a single helpful reminder that ends the workflow after sending.

quizzes.question: Does a fixed Wait action automatically know when someone has booked an appointment?

options.option_text: Yes, Wait automatically stops when a booking is detected
No; you must configure booking or reply checks explicitly
Only if the calendar is integrated with LeadProspectrr
Yes, but only for appointments booked through the workflow link

quizzes.explanation: A simple Wait action does not automatically stop messages when someone books. You must explicitly configure reply checks, booking checks, or removal logic in the workflow.

quizzes.question: What are two valid reasons to stop a follow-up reminder?

options.option_text: The contact opened the email and clicked a link
The contact replied or booked an appointment
The contact visited your website
The contact downloaded a PDF

quizzes.explanation: If a contact has replied to your email or booked an appointment, they have engaged and should not receive a sales reminder. Other actions like opening an email or visiting a website do not necessarily indicate engagement.

quizzes.question: How many reminder emails should the workflow send?

options.option_text: Three reminders over one week
One helpful reminder, then end the workflow
Unlimited until the contact responds
Two reminders: one at 1 day and one at 3 days

quizzes.explanation: Send one helpful reminder, then end the workflow. A separate Customer Booked Appointment workflow can handle confirmations and reminders for appointments.

title: Test, publish and monitor
learningGoal: Make the process reliable before a real prospect sees it.

items.title: Submit the Form
items.description: Submit the selected form using a test email address.

items.title: Confirm Contact Record
items.description: Check that the expected contact record appears in Contacts.

items.title: Check Workflow Enrollment
items.description: Verify the workflow enrollment and the email in Conversations and/or workflow execution history.

items.title: Verify Email Delivery
items.description: Check that the email is delivered and the booking link opens the intended calendar.

items.title: No-Response Scenario
items.description: The single reminder is sent after the configured wait.

items.title: Reply Scenario
items.description: Subsequent sales reminder is suppressed when the contact replies.

items.title: Booking Scenario
items.description: Subsequent sales reminder is suppressed when the contact books.

items.title: Opt-outs Respected
items.description: Confirm opt-outs and workflow settings are respected.

items.title: Publish After Testing
items.description: Publish and save only after all testing is successful.

items.title: Exercise for Service Businesses
items.description: Write down who in your team should get a notification when an enquiry is submitted or a call is booked.

keyPoint: Test three scenarios before publishing: no response (reminder sends), reply (reminder suppressed), and booking (reminder suppressed). Only publish after successful end-to-end testing.

actionSteps.title: Submit a test form
actionSteps.description: Use a test email address to submit your enquiry form and confirm the contact record appears.

actionSteps.title: Test the no-response path
actionSteps.description: Wait for the configured time and confirm the reminder email sends correctly.

actionSteps.title: Test reply and booking paths
actionSteps.description: Verify that replying or booking suppresses the reminder email.

quizzes.question: When should you publish the workflow?

options.option_text: Immediately after creating it
After successful end-to-end testing
After adding the first email
When the first real enquiry comes in

quizzes.explanation: Publish and save only after all testing is successful. Publishing before testing risks sending incorrect or incomplete follow-ups to real prospects.

quizzes.question: What should you test besides the email wording?

options.option_text: Only the subject line
Form filter, delivery, merge fields, link, timing, booking and reply exits, opt-outs
Only the booking link
Only the wait time

quizzes.explanation: Test the form filter, email delivery, merge fields, booking link, wait timing, booking and reply exit paths, and opt-out handling. The email wording is only one part of a reliable follow-up journey.

quizzes.question: How many test scenarios should you run before publishing?

options.option_text: One: submit the form
Three: no response, reply, and booked appointment
Five: one for each step of the formula
Two: form submission and email delivery

quizzes.explanation: Run three tests: no response (reminder sends), reply (reminder suppressed), and booked appointment (reminder suppressed). This ensures all paths work correctly before going live.

title: Improve based on real conversations
learningGoal: Track whether the journey helps clients take the next step.

items.title: Enquiry Form Submissions
items.description: Count how many forms were submitted each week.

items.title: First Emails Successfully Sent
items.description: Track delivery and identify any sending failures.

items.title: Replies and Bookings
items.description: Measure replies and appointment bookings attributable to those enquiries.

items.title: Unsubscribes and Complaints
items.description: Monitor unsubscribes, complaints, and duplicate follow-ups.

items.title: Common Questions
items.description: Identify questions that the first email could answer better.

items.title: Do Not Compare Raw Counts Alone
items.description: Do not compare raw booking counts without also considering the number and quality of enquiries.

items.title: Start with an Observation
items.description: Notice a pattern, make one small change, then check results.

items.title: Exercise for Coaches
items.description: If many people reply with questions but few book, what could you change about the email? Write one answer that helps the prospect before asking them to book.

keyPoint: Review weekly: form submissions, emails sent, replies, bookings, unsubscribes, and common questions. Do not compare raw booking counts without considering enquiry quality. Make one small change at a time.

actionSteps.title: Set up weekly tracking
actionSteps.description: Create a simple tracker for form submissions, emails sent, replies, bookings, and unsubscribes.

actionSteps.title: Review common questions
actionSteps.description: Look at replies and identify questions your first email could answer better.

actionSteps.title: Make one small improvement
actionSteps.description: Choose one change to test — a clearer subject line, a better booking link placement, or an added FAQ sentence.

quizzes.question: What should you review weekly to improve your follow-up journey?

options.option_text: Only the number of bookings
Form submissions, emails sent, replies, bookings, unsubscribes, and common questions
Only the workflow execution history
Only the calendar availability

quizzes.explanation: Review form submissions, first emails sent, replies and bookings, unsubscribes and complaints, and common questions. This gives a complete picture of how the journey is performing.

quizzes.question: Why should you not compare raw booking counts alone?

options.option_text: Because bookings are not important
Because you must also consider the number and quality of enquiries
Because the workflow does not track bookings
Because booking counts are always inaccurate

quizzes.explanation: Raw booking counts without context can be misleading. A drop in bookings might reflect fewer or lower-quality enquiries, not a broken follow-up process. Always consider enquiry volume and quality.

quizzes.question: What is the recommended approach to improving the follow-up journey?

options.option_text: Redesign the entire workflow every week
Start with an observation, make one small change, then check results
Copy a competitor's workflow exactly
Add more emails and reminders

quizzes.explanation: Start with an observation from your weekly review, make one small change, then check results. This controlled approach helps you understand what actually improves performance.
